assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only three-days-of-happiness:himeno@original-novel#novel-monograph (the canonical v1.0 Himeno novel monograph, qualified COMPLETE_AT_BOUNDARY (bounded), accepted with corrections and passed on receiving review against the Japanese EPUB) at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the single Japanese witness TDH-JP-01, native chapters 1-15, end paratext excluded. Himeno speaks in person only in Ch01, Ch09 P0147 and Ch10; the rest is traces, Kusunoki's constructions and Miyagi's testimony, which the monograph separates from her own words and which this assessment does not treat as evidence of her. The readings, the longitudinal notebook, the novel synthesis, the completion audit, the release-decision record and the other monographs are not cited, and nothing is borrowed from them. The audit's readiness table, its RETROSPECTIVE_CONSISTENCY_TEST caution and the project's statement that no reconstruction operation is authorized were read as method inputs, not conclusions. No translation, adaptation or other edition is assessed, and the evaluator inspected no primary source.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Three located periods only, as the monograph's profile defines them: V10, age ten (the classroom answer, the shrine scene Ch01 P0057-P0093 and narrated childhood, with childhood memories recalled at twenty used as her or his testimony as labeled); V17, her letter at seventeen, known only through Kusunoki's summary (Ch09 P0054-P0063); and V20, the festival-night encounter (Ch09 P0136-P0148; Ch10 P0004-P0008) and the dinner day (Ch10 P0080-P0154), with her letter (Ch10 P0190-P0200) as her testimony about intentions up to the dinner. The dinner is split at her decision to abandon the plan, made by strong inference within minutes of his confession (Ch10 P0137-P0151). Her life between ten and twenty is known only as disputed summary facts, and nothing after her exit from the dinner is established.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph gives a specialist account of Himeno's values, goals, fears, coping and self-conception at ten and at twenty (sections 8-9): rank, wealth, others' envy and a balanced ledger at ten (Ch01 P0070-P0074); at twenty her own self-diagnosis of arrested growth and intolerance of imperfection (Ch10 P0134) and, in her letter, a stated mechanism: an unanswered call for help, resentment, a plan of revenge through becoming indispensable and dying before him, and its abandonment as pointless once he seems already broken (Ch10 P0193-P0197). Counterevidence: the mechanism is one letter of testimony; whether her warmth at dinner was sincere or strategic is undecidable (TDH-S054), as are whether she believed the prophecy or meant the proposal at ten. Not B: being unable to tell which motive drives her only adult conduct is insufficiency, not productive uncertainty. Not D: values are located, and her own causal statements give an explicit, if testimonial, account of the change.

Two narrated periods ten years apart, with one summarized letter at seventeen between them. The monograph separates what changed (her orientation to Kusunoki, from the shared 私たち at ten to 私 against あなた in the letter; her fortune; her self-understanding), what persisted (the ledger logic, pride and self-cover, framing others), and what was only revealed late (her secret admiration of his drawings), and locates one change in real time, the abandonment of her plan at the dinner (section 16). Not C: development cannot be followed continuously; the decade, the date of the grievance and when the plan formed are unstated, and her decade's facts come from two partly conflicting sources. Not E: change and persistence are located at both ends with a stated cause.

Himeno's written Japanese is documented by context with anchors (section 11): polite です/ます in class (Ch01 P0009); plain declaratives with soft endings and 私たち in private at ten (Ch01 P0063-P0074); halting plain speech switching to polite 〜ませんか and back to 忘れてちょうだい at the proposal (Ch01 P0087-P0092); casual, quick teasing with クスノキ and 君, 正直でよろしい, ふうん, なるほど at twenty (Ch10 P0090-P0149); written polite 私/あなた with malefactive てやる in the letter. Recurrent markers (そっか, apologetic preambles, self-cover jokes, a market idiom for persons) are located. Counterevidence: each context is one scene or one document, all inside Kusunoki's record, and Ch01 is recalled about ten years later. Not B: the sample is too small to fix register under pressures not shown. Not D: a context-by-context register system with recurrent, located markers.

The monograph states that her supported preferences and habits are few (section 13): carrying an umbrella as a child, admiring and secretly keeping his drawings, citing a book at ten, declining alcohol at twenty for an unstated reason, staying home at ten and going out on festival days for the parents' sake, a car and work in the area at twenty, lateness with an apology and an offer to pay. Food, clothing, leisure, music and daily routine are unknown at both ages. Not D: these are isolated, mostly single items without a routine.

Toward Kusunoki the monograph traces four stages (at ten, at seventeen, at the dinner, in the letter; section 12) with a stated cause of change and a grammatical trace of it, and analyses the asymmetry of what each knew. Other relations are one-line: classmates (mutual contempt), parents (the friendship performance, narrated summary), the teacher (one exchange), husband and child (summary facts, the child only by Miyagi's testimony). Not C: only one relationship is sampled, its adult stage is undecidable between sincerity and strategy, and the seventeen-year-old stage is known through his summary. Not E: the Kusunoki relation is located at two ages with a stated reason for its reversal.

Himeno's interior is never narrated. The only direct access is her letter at twenty, which the monograph treats as testimony about past intention, not narrated interiority, and her dinner self-diagnosis, given while her purpose was concealed; the narrator's readings of her feelings ("like another person," "the eyes of a hurt girl") are marked as his (sections 5, 7, 11). Her inner state at any moment is an explicit abstention zone (section 17). Not D: two items of testimony, not distributed disclosure.

A consistent indirectness is located at both ages (section 10): covert, physical rivalry under the table at ten (Ch01 P0043, narrated summary); at twenty no confrontation at dinner, the implausibility of his story named gently before a profession of belief (Ch10 P0147-P0149), hostility planned and concealed, then stated in writing after she has gone, through the waiter (Ch10 P0151-P0200). Not C: each adult case is a single instance, and her hostility is known only from her letter. Not E: the same indirect pattern recurs across both periods.

The monograph states that no conflicting obligation is depicted from her side (section 9). The one located datum is the letter's reasoning: she abandons revenge because it seems pointless against a man already stranger than she, not because it is wrong, and does not forgive him (Ch10 P0196-P0198); capacity and willingness are separated there (section 15). At ten she gives the classroom's lifetime-earnings price of a life by citing a book (Ch01 P0009). Not D: one testimonial instance of reasoning about an act, with no deliberation shown.

Forms are located at both ages (sections 5, 7, 11): dry, competitive play at ten (the classmates' envy heart attacks, Ch01 P0072-P0074); self-cover jokes after exposure (冗談だよ, and the boast that she could hardly be left over, Ch01 P0092); teasing at twenty (うそつき in answer to the truth, 正直でよろしい with a giggle, the prim ふうん; Ch10 P0093-P0104); and a barb closing the letter (P0200). Not C: a handful of instances in two scenes. Not E: self-cover and teasing reversal recur across both periods.

The novel is complete, and the monograph covers every chapter in which Himeno is present or referred to (Ch01-Ch15), with an explicit table of evidence classes from her letter and recorded speech down to Kusunoki's constructions and Miyagi's testimony (section 1), locators throughout and a traceability table to readings and notebook IDs (section 19), after acceptance with corrections and a receiving review against the Japanese EPUB, according to the discovery row. Not A: one derived synthesis whose locators resolve outside the cited set, under reviews the project calls bounded. Not C: whole-work coverage separated by kind of evidence.

The evidence affirmatively bounds Himeno: Miyagi's testimony about her is itemized by standing, with "barely remembers you" shown false by strong inference and an unspecified admitted lie about her (Ch12 P0193; section 4.2); Kusunoki's decoding of her letter at seventeen as an SOS and his "she will soon kill herself" are shown to be his inferences with listed weaknesses (section 6); counterexamples to four simple portraits, rival explanations and unresolved contradictions are listed (section 18); and abstention zones are explicit (section 17). Not A: several bounds are unknowns the text never had occasion to settle. Not C: located refutations and contradictions, not only silences.

Himeno's states are located by age and period (V10, V17, V20), by a history table that records for each event its source, standing, chapter of disclosure and what Kusunoki knew at the time (section 3), and by the located decision within the dinner. The composition chronology of Kusunoki's record is stated as a limit. Not A: the order of shrine, capsule and transfer within the summer at ten is not given, the order of her childbirth, dropout and marriage is disputed between sources, and when the grievance and the plan formed is unstated. Not C: an explicit, anchored sequence with disclosure order.

conditions: Illustrative textual Japanese only, never quotation, and only toward Kusunoki in a situation closely resembling one shown: V10 private talk (plain declaratives, soft endings, 私 and 私たち, no names or second-person pronouns) or V20 sociable talk at the dinner (casual, quick, teasing; クスノキ and 君; そっか; apologetic preambles before frank content).
Polite register only where the evidence places it: a classroom answer, or a marked moment of exposure followed by retraction; no letter text is generated.
Lines express surface conduct only: no stated motive, belief in his story, romantic feeling, view of the childhood promise, or account of her decade beyond the summary facts she gave.
Nothing after her exit from the dinner (Ch10 P0154), and nothing toward anyone else after ten.
scenario_readiness.note: Himeno's register is documented by context, so short lines in the two sampled settings are constrained in form. Each setting is one scene, and her motive at the dinner is undecidable, so the use is narrow and surface-level.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One located period only: V10 (Ch01 and narrated childhood), or V20 from the festival-night encounter (Ch09 P0136) to her exit from the dinner (Ch10 P0154), before or after her decision there; V17 is known only through his summary.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Kusunoki as childhood rival and friend at ten, or as the friend she meets again at twenty while concealing a grievance; the teacher and parents only as in the summarized childhood scenes. Miyagi, whom she cannot perceive, her husband, her child, colleagues and anyone after ten are excluded.
setting_constraints: The novel's world and its hometown places as located: the classroom, the shrine steps, the families' houses, the restaurant.
No work, family life or other setting from her decade.

scenario_readiness.note: Every row of the monograph's conditional profile rests on one scene, one summary or one letter, and the motive behind her only adult conduct is undecidable between sincerity and strategy. A materially novel scenario would require choosing her motive, which would be invention; the monograph itself confines use to close analogy with the shrine or the dinner.
One dinner and a few childhood habits are located, and her everyday life at both ages is unknown; the dinner's warmth is undecidable between sincerity and strategy.
No deliberation by Himeno is shown; the only reasoning about an act is her letter's judgment that revenge had become pointless. Ethical reasoning in a new situation would be invention.

At ten the source shows only a conditional proposal, marked by embarrassment and retracted as a joke; at twenty her letter makes becoming indispensable to him instrumental to revenge, and the monograph adopts no romantic reading of the dinner. Her intimate preferences and her marriage are not shown.
Her work at twenty is unknown beyond her evasive "work dealing with people"; no work conduct is recorded.

known_limits.statement: In her own person Himeno is shown in two concentrated sequences (Ch01; Ch09 P0136 to Ch10 P0200), one classroom answer and one letter; her decade between ten and twenty is never shown.

Because her letter discloses a plan to become indispensable to Kusunoki before dying in front of him, every warm act at the dinner, including her professed belief in his story, is undecidable between sincerity and strategy (TDH-S054).
Her letter at twenty is her own written testimony about past intention; its truth, sincerity and completeness are not independently checked, and when the plan formed is not stated.

All of Himeno's speech and conduct reaches the page through Kusunoki's record, written by strong inference after her letter; the ten-year-old's portrait is recalled about ten years later, and its touches of vulnerability cannot be checked for retrospective coloring (TDH-C010).

Kusunoki's dream, imagined letters, retelling and decoding, and Miyagi's account of her life and original course, are evidence of their Himenos, not of her; Miyagi's account stands item by item, and she admits an unspecified lie about Himeno (Ch12 P0193).
Himeno's fate is never narrated; Miyagi's original-course forecast is uncorroborated except as the plan Himeno says she abandoned, and Kusunoki's "she will soon kill herself" is his belief.
The cited evidence contains no reconstruction model, probe or held-out evaluation of Himeno; the monograph's conditional profile is a literary aid it states has not been tested.
